title: Diogenes the Wise Man
attribution: Excerpted (trimmed) from "Diogenes the Wise Man" in Fifty Famous Stories Retold by James Baldwin (1896), via Project Gutenberg. Syllable-break hyphens from the original edition's typesetting (e.g., "Di-og'e-nes," "Cor-inth") have been corrected, and two short paragraphs have been merged.
body: At Corinth, in Greece, there lived a very wise man whose name was Diogenes. Men came from all parts of the land to see him and hear him talk.

But wise as he was, he had some very queer ways. He did not believe that any man ought to have more things than he really needed; and he said that no man needed much. And so he did not live in a house, but slept in a tub or barrel, which he rolled about from place to place.
At noon one day, Diogenes was seen walking through the streets with a lighted lantern, and looking all around as if in search of something.
"Why do you carry a lantern when the sun is shining?" some one said.
"I am looking for an honest man," answered Diogenes.

When Alexander the Great went to Corinth, all the foremost men in the city came out to see him and to praise him. But Diogenes did not come; and he was the only man for whose opinions Alexander cared.

And so, since the wise man would not come to see the king, the king went to see the wise man. He found Diogenes in an out-of-the-way place, lying on the ground by his tub. He was enjoying the heat and the light of the sun.

When he saw the king and a great many people coming, he sat up and looked at Alexander. Alexander greeted him and said, "Diogenes, I have heard a great deal about your wisdom. Is there anything that I can do for you?"
"Yes," said Diogenes. "You can stand a little on one side, so as not to keep the sunshine from me."

This answer was so different from what he expected, that the king was much surprised. But it did not make him angry; it only made him admire the strange man all the more. When he turned to ride back, he said to his officers, "Say what you will; if I were not Alexander, I would like to be Diogenes."

questions.prompt: According to the passage, in what city did Diogenes live?
options: Athens
Sparta
Corinth
Thebes

questions.prompt: According to the passage, where did Diogenes sleep instead of in a house?
options: In a tub or barrel
Under a bridge
In a cave outside the city
In the marketplace

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what was Diogenes carrying as he walked through the streets at noon?
options: A wooden staff
A bundle of scrolls
A jug of water
A lighted lantern

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does Diogenes say he is looking for with his lantern?
options: A missing coin
An honest man
A place to sleep
His pet dog

questions.prompt: According to the passage, why does Alexander go to see Diogenes instead of the other way around?
options: Diogenes was too old to travel to the palace
Alexander wanted to see the famous tub for himself
Diogenes did not come to see Alexander, so Alexander went to him
Diogenes had sent Alexander a written invitation

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does Diogenes ask Alexander to do for him?
options: Stand a little on one side so as not to block the sunshine
Give him a warmer cloak for the winter
Build him a proper house in Corinth
Send him food from the royal kitchen

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does Alexander say to his officers as he rides back?
options: "That man should be thrown out of Corinth"
"Bring him a proper house at once"
"He has insulted me before my own men"
"If I were not Alexander, I would like to be Diogenes"

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does Diogenes search for an honest man in broad daylight with a lantern?
options: Because he cannot see well without extra light
To make the point that honest men are rare enough to need searching for
Because he has lost something valuable nearby
Because it is a custom among the wise men of Corinth

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why is Alexander surprised rather than angry at Diogenes's request?
options: He did not expect Diogenes to speak to him at all
He believed Diogenes did not know who he was
He expected Diogenes to ask for wealth or favor, not simply for sunlight
He thought Diogenes would ask to join his army

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does it mean that Diogenes had some "queer" ways?
options: Unusual or strange habits
Dishonest or deceitful habits
Cruel or unkind habits
Careless or lazy habits

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did Diogenes believe about how many things a man needs?
options: That every man needs a house of his own
That wealth is the true mark of wisdom
That a man needs as much as a king
That no man needs very much

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how did the foremost men of Corinth treat Alexander when he arrived?
options: They refused to leave their homes
They came out to see him and to praise him
They asked him to leave the city at once
They sent Diogenes to greet him instead

questions.prompt: According to the passage, where does Alexander find Diogenes?
options: Sitting in the city's marketplace
Standing at the gates of Corinth
Lying on the ground by his tub, in an out-of-the-way place
Walking along the seashore

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does Alexander offer to do for Diogenes when they meet?
options: Anything Diogenes might ask of him
Build him a marble tub to replace the old one
Appoint him as an adviser to the army
Grant him a place among the foremost men

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does Diogenes choose to live in a tub rather than a house?
options: He cannot afford to build himself a house
The city of Corinth forbids him from owning property
He wants to travel and a tub is easy to roll about
It fits his belief that no one truly needs more than very little

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does it mean that Diogenes lived in an "out-of-the-way" place?
options: A place at the very center of the city
A spot away from where most people usually went
A place forbidden to ordinary citizens
A place known only to kings

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: A philosopher begs a king for a proper house to live in
A king punishes a philosopher for refusing to greet him
A king offers a poor philosopher anything, and the philosopher asks only to be left alone in the sun
A philosopher joins Alexander's army after their meeting
